newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: OLYMPICS-WHITES OPPOSE S.AFRICA GOVERNMENT SPENDING ON BID.
newsitem.headline: OLYMPICS-WHITES OPPOSE S.AFRICA GOVERNMENT SPENDING ON BID.

text.p: The majority of white South Africans oppose government spending on Cape Town's bid for the 2000 Olympics, an independent survey has revealed.
The survey said blacks and Asians polled were most supportive with 74 per cent and 75 per cent respectively supporting government involvement.
However, among the country's minority white population only 47 per cent supported the idea.
"We are disappointed that the level of white support still doesn't match that of other groups in the country and city," Ameen Akhalwaya, media director of the Cape Town bid, said in a statement.
"But the latest poll confirms that the vast majority of South Africans are convinced of the huge economic and development benefits of staging the Olympics here.
